lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- The Lunch
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Mauricio | Lesson 9 -- The Lunch

listenings.text: If you ask me what I got out of that fortnight, the honest answer is not the sessions. The sessions were good, and I have forgotten most of them. What I still have, four years later, is six people. One of them I call whenever I have to fire somebody, because he is better at it than I am. One of them sent me a spreadsheet last month that saved my team three weeks. And I met all six of them at lunch, not in a session. So my advice, if you want it: the sessions are the reason you are there, and the lunches are the reason it was worth it. You should sit somewhere different every day. It might feel uncomfortable on day one. Do it anyway.

One warning about networking, because everybody gets this wrong at least once. There is always somebody who works the room, collects forty cards, and goes home with nothing. And there is always somebody quiet who has three real conversations and goes home with three people who will answer an email. Be the second one. Two practical things. First, when the conversation ends, say what you will do next, and be specific: not let us keep in touch, but I will send you that article on Thursday. Second, actually send it. That is it. That is the whole method. The people who are good at this are not more charming than you. They just follow up.
